document_summary: A composite recording. The opening uses Sura 61 to discuss saying what one does not do, supporting God's cause, and victory beginning in worldly life. An unidentified male teacher then moves through Suras 87, 88, and 89, including creation, pasture, Hell and Paradise, dawn, ten nights, Ad, Thamud, Pharaoh, material provision, orphans, and charity. Rashad discusses Sura 94, striving, charity, provision, and happiness, then references Sura 92 and Sura 93. Edip leads the final and longest block on Sura 81: cosmic collapse, resurrection, buried girls, animals, oppression of women, and the Messenger of the Covenant. Rashad applies verses 81:19–24 to himself, presents several numerical calculations, recounts being acknowledged by all prophets at a high horizon, and describes the first generation as the elite of the elite.

sections.title: Sura 61: saying what one does not do, supporting God, and victory here and now
sections.summary: The opening discusses Quran 61:1–13. Believers should not say what they fail to practice, should form a solid structure in God's cause, and should support God as Jesus' disciples did. The promised victory is interpreted as beginning in worldly life rather than being postponed entirely to the Hereafter.
